steps.question: What should control corners say?
steps.why: Rounded by default; each brand sets its own corner.
Labels stay readable in every brand.
Customers are often on phones.
Each brand sets its own corner through the theme.

pick: radius.4: We use a 4px corner for Aster's buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a calm, precise tone, by brand convention. A small radius does this by softening the edge just enough while the sides stay straight. So Aster feels exact and steady, the least round of the three brands, because each brand sets its corners (shape.values) on a neutral base (brand.q1).

steps.question: What rises above the page?
steps.why: Cards lift slightly to group offers.

steps.question: How soft are shadows?
steps.why: Soft shadows fit every brand.
The shadow shows a menu or dialog floats above the page. Without it, it blends into the cards.

steps.rule: Fills that float above content. In dark, one step lighter than content, so height reads by tone.
pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.
darkPick: neutral.100: We use one step lighter than content for menus, dialogs and raised cards in dark, in order to show height by tone,

on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. So customers see a menu above the page even where its shadow barely shows, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

pick: shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show floating height, one step above the cards. The cast shade does this by a 12px offset and a 32px blur at 16%, four times the card's blur. So a menu floats clear above the cards in every brand, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and shadows are soft (elevation.values).
darkPick: shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light overlay shadow's shape in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 12px offset and 32px blur, at 50% black instead of 16%. So a menu still floats above the cards, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and dark ships for every brand (theming.values).

pick: radius.8: We use an 8px corner for Aster's cards and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a calm tone by brand convention. A modest radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve twice the 4px control corner. So a plan card reads as one object without feeling soft, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and each brand colors a neutral base (brand.q1).

steps.rule: The 1px edge of a raised layer. In dark, a solid step lighter than the raised surface, so the edge shows where a shadow cannot.
pick: neutral.200: We use the default line's step for the edge of menus, dialogs and other raised layers, in order to give separation between a layer and what lies under it. The ring does this by a 1px line,

on surface.raised, beside the light shadow that does most of the lift. So customers see where a menu ends on any page, because raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).
darkPick: neutral.200: We use the step above the raised surface for a 1px ring around raised layers in dark, in order to give separation where a shadow barely shows. The ring does this by a solid, lighter line,

on surface.raised (#334155, no alpha), so its contrast can be checked. So customers see a dark menu's edge on any page, because dark ships as standard (theming.values), raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surfaces it sits on: darker in light, and darker in dark too, as raised layers take the lighter step.
pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
darkPick: neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the canvas, for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on both surfaces it meets:
on surface.default and
on surface.raised, and
off the page. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads
on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).
